appearance_facts.fact: The orange bar's top edge is positioned slightly above the 50 mark on the vertical axis.
The dark blue bar is the tallest mark on the page, with its top edge positioned slightly above the 60 mark on the vertical axis.
The light blue bar's top edge is positioned between the 40 and 50 marks on the vertical axis.
The orange-yellow bar is the second shortest mark, with its top edge positioned just below the 10 mark on the vertical axis.
The red bar is the shortest mark on the page, with its top edge positioned below the 10 mark on the vertical axis.
Visually, the dark blue Safari bar extends significantly higher on the page than the orange Chrome bar, which in turn is higher than the light blue Edge bar.

printed_facts.fact: The text 'Browser Usage Share by Product' appears in the upper left corner.
The vertical axis is labeled with numerical values ranging from 0 to 100 in increments of 10.
The horizontal axis lists the categories: Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox, and Others.
The text '38%' is printed directly above the orange Chrome bar.
The text '4%' is printed directly above the dark blue Safari bar.
The text '44%' is printed directly above the light blue Edge bar.
The text '4%' is printed directly above the orange-yellow Firefox bar.
The text '10%' is printed directly above the red Others bar.

public_definitions: Select the browser with the highest current market_share
Business reason: Highest-usage browser has the largest support load and user-impact surface
uncertain: There is a visual conflict: the Safari bar is the tallest on the chart (indicating the highest value), but its printed label is '4%'.
The printed label for Edge ('44%') is numerically higher than the label for Chrome ('38%'), but the Edge bar is visually shorter than the Chrome bar.
